title: Symmetry-Projected Compatible Multiparameter Quantum Sensing
authors: G. R. Jin, Z. Y. Zhou, W. Yang
abstract: We establish a general symmetry-projection framework for multiparameter quantum sensing. Decomposing encoding generators into subspace-preserving and subspace-changing components relative to a symmetry sector identically eliminates all cross-sector elements of the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) and the mean symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) commutator matrix. When projected subspace-changing generators act as a scalar within the occupied subspace, the corresponding QFIM block reduces to four times the symmetrized covariance matrix, regardless of probe state purity. For parity-protected collective $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ spin systems, this renders the transverse QFIM directly certifiable via spin fluctuations, with the optimal axis aligned with the anti-squeezed quadrature. Applied to a dissipative one-axis-twisting system, our framework reveals that highly mixed transient states can exhibit nearly balanced, Heisenberg-scaled QFIM components for transverse--longitudinal parameter pairs $(θ_y,θ_z)$ over a broad time window. Furthermore, while the steady state retains an isotropic transverse QFIM scaling as $N^2/3$, weak compatibility for transverse parameter pairs $(θ_x,θ_y)$ exhibits a sharp parity dependence---failing for odd $N$ but restored for even $N$. The resulting symmetry protection eliminates the Uhlmann curvature for transverse--longitudinal pairs, enabling simultaneous saturation of the multi-parameter quantum Cramér-Rao bound in the asymptotic limit.
summary: The paper introduces a symmetry-projection framework for multiparameter quantum sensing that mathematically guarantees the decoupling of parameter information sectors. By restricting analysis to states within a symmetry sector, it shows how cross-talk terms vanish in the QFIM, enabling simultaneous and optimal estimation of multiple parameters even in dissipative systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving simultaneous information-sector decoupling and weak compatibility between multiple parameters ($	heta_{\alpha}$) in quantum sensing, which are often hindered by statistical coupling.
main_result: A symmetry-projection framework was developed that guarantees the vanishing of cross-sector elements in the Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM) and SLD commutators, leading to decoupled and weakly compatible parameter estimation channels.
method: The authors decompose encoding generators relative to a symmetry sector projector ($\hat{P}$) into subspace-preserving and changing components. They then calculate the QFIM and use these restricted operators to derive analytical conditions for decoupling.
model_or_system: The framework is applied generally but features specific models including parity-protected collective SU(2) spin systems (N spins) and dissipative One-Axis-Twisting (OAT) dynamics. The analysis focuses on probe states confined to a symmetry sector ($\hat{ho} = \hat{P}\hat{ho}\hat{P}$).
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information Matrix (QFIM), mean Symmetric Logarithmic Derivative (SLD) commutator matrix, Uhlmann curvature, and spin fluctuation variances.
important_parameters: The number of particles ($N$), the parity of $N$ (even vs. odd), and the time evolution parameters ($	heta_x, 	heta_y, 	heta_z$).
main_assumptions: The analysis fundamentally relies on restricting the probe state to a symmetry-projected subspace ($\hat{ho} = \hat{P}\hat{ho}\hat{P}$), which simplifies the full compatibility problem.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of various QFI components under dissipative OAT dynamics, showing plateaus and suppression due to dephasing effects.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general symmetry-projection framework by decomposing generators. It then applies this to specific systems like SU(2) spins and OAT models, deriving conditions for cross-term vanishing (decoupling) and weak compatibility using spin correlation measurements.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool—symmetry protection—to simplify complex multi-parameter quantum estimation problems in interacting quantum systems, directly linking fundamental symmetries to measurable metrological advantages.
